title: Counting the Wings
request: How many books belong to each wing? One row per wing, wings in alphabetical order, and the tally column named count.
objective: Group rows by a categorical column to count them.
hints: A wing that appears nine times still deserves exactly one row in the tally.
group collapses repeated values of one column and adds a count column on its own.
Group the cart on the wing column and sort the grouped table by wing before delivering it.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
wings = ['Reference', 'Nature', 'Travel', 'Poetry', 'Mystery']
titles = ['Lanterns of the Slow Tide', 'Winter Comes to the Aviary', 'Nine Ways to Fold a Map', 'The Brass Hour', 'Eleven Rooms of Rain', 'The Lamp Under the Stair', 'Salt and Moss and Patience', 'Instructions for Slow Travel', 'The Index of Small Storms']
n = random.randint(4, 9)
picked = random.sample(titles, n)
shelf = Table().with_columns('title', make_array(*picked), 'wing', make_array(*[random.choice(wings) for _ in range(n)]))

rows: Nine Ways to Fold a Map
